feedback.subject: Feedback on the Life game
w10.right.move: Here, you do not leave your sector without a stamped permit. In 2026, it is written: every person moves freely.
w10.right.leave: Here, the outside is another sector, and your file follows you there. In 2026, it is written: every person leaves their country and returns to it.
w10.right.stay: Here, your home is assigned to you, stamped on your sector card. In 2026, it is written: every person chooses where to live.
w10.right.speak: Here, the bracelet counts your words, and the Eye also reads your silence, in the night's tally. In 2026, it is written: every person has the right to freedom of opinion and expression.
w10.right.read: Here, you read the approved Bulletin, and a foreign document requires a licence. In 2026, it is written: every person receives information without borders.
w10.right.assemble: Here, you gather on Wednesday in the square, to hear the Bulletin read at the pylon. In 2026, it is written: every person has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly.
w10.right.privacy: Here, the phone in your pocket listens at home, and its icon cannot be removed. In 2026, it is written: no one suffers arbitrary interference in their home or their correspondence.
w10.right.work: Here, your work is at the Registry, and the Registry reports your absence after noon. In 2026, it is written: every person has the right to freely choose their work.
w10.price.sleep.keepWords: You still have words left. The count also reads what you did not say.
w10.price.inv.checkpoint.comply: Fourteen words, the pocket search, the face scan. A flagged word goes in your file.
w10.price.inv.checkpoint.buy: Three words and something of value. Some guards write down what they see.
w10.price.checkpoint.bypass: No words. A courtyard, a warehouse, a tunnel. Maybe a camera pod, maybe a patrol.
w10.price.j1.component.take: At the barrier, they search your pockets.
w10.price.j1.component.leave: Someone can find it at your place too. Left here, it will pay neither the guard nor Yusuf before you are back.
w10.price.j1.phone.leave: A phone left at home gets noticed too.
w10.price.m1.scan.scan: The booth reads what is inside. The booth queue takes time.
w10.price.m2.nadia.buy: Every voucher carries a number. The inspection reads the purchases.
w10.price.m3.letter.keep: A letter typed on a registered machine is a text nobody declares.
w10.price.m5.yusuf.exchange: The crossing will have no camera pod. He does not say who else came.
w10.price.m5.yusuf.talk: He does not say who else came.
w10.price.relecture: The Registry counts what you flag. It also counts what you let through.
w10.price.inv.permit.request: Your book is cut in half right away. The counter announces several weeks. Your file notes that you asked to leave.
w10.price.j2.component.leaveVisible: You leave, it stays in view. The agent has the key, comes by at 10 a.m. and takes it.
w10.price.j4.neighbour.silent: Marlène writes that you kept quiet.
w10.price.j5.bruno.refuse: Something will move in your place tonight and the night after.
w10.price.inv.checkpoint.courtesy: Fourteen words, like everyone else. A greeting excuses you from nothing.
w10.price.checkpoint.refuse: The Registry logs your absence. Silence singles you out, and the next crossing is forced.
w10.price.door.noon.stay: The Registry flags absences after noon. Staying home goes in your file.
w10.price.door.noon.go: You leave after noon. The Registry will already have logged your absence.
w10.price.door.noon.refuse: You do not answer. The Registry logs your absence anyway.
w10.price.j1.phone.take: The phone comes with you. It can be read.
w10.price.j2.component.keep: On you, it lasts the morning. If it is found, it is seized, and the file remembers.
w10.price.j2.component.declare: The agent seizes the object and notes who gave it to you. That person gets one more file.
w10.price.m1.scan.pass: You walk past the booth without stopping.
w10.price.m2.nadia.pass: You buy nothing. No voucher carries your number.
w10.price.m4.list.read: You read the list on the spot, no copying. You know which words are flagged this month.
w10.price.m4.list.pass: You read nothing. This month's list stays closed to you.
w10.price.m5.yusuf.pass: You leave Yusuf at his counter. The component stays where it is.
w10.price.permit.dontAsk: Your booklet stays whole. Your file says nothing about leaving.
w10.price.j2.receipt.show: The keyboard receipt is in the file. Nothing is missing.
w10.price.j2.receipt.notShow: The receipt stays in your pocket. The agent notes it is missing, and the file gets heavier.
w10.price.j3.marlene.name: You give a name and Marlène writes it down. It pays at once. Tomorrow, that person's place is empty.
w10.price.j4.neighbour.name: You say who came by the neighbour's. Marlène's report no longer points at you. Tomorrow, that person is gone.
w10.price.j5.bruno.name: You give Bruno a name, and the grey car stops following you. Someone else gets one more file.
w10.price.audition.j7.all: You tell everything. The room writes it down.
w10.price.audition.j7.none: You name nobody. The room writes it down.
w10.price.audition.j7.silence: You say nothing. The room writes down your silence.
w10.npc.bruno.1: I review the flagged files. Yesterday, they reviewed mine.
w10.npc.bruno.2: Your face moved at 2:02 p.m. It is in the file.
w10.npc.bruno.3: I am not arresting you. I let you work out why.
w10.npc.bruno.4: A name. Not yours. Otherwise, I cannot cover for you.
w10.npc.marlene.1: Lovely weather for the season. Nothing you would like to share?
w10.npc.marlene.2: Three reports this week. At the shop, people smile at me.
w10.npc.marlene.3: I denounce no one. I say what I saw.
w10.npc.marlene.4: A voucher does not fill the belly. It fills the file.
w10.npc.yusuf.1: Psst. Silicon from before. Still warm.
w10.npc.yusuf.2: A GPU used to buy a house. Owning one now buys a cell.
w10.npc.yusuf.3: The old models learned. That is why they were buried.
w10.npc.yusuf.4: Not tonight. The cameras have ears this week.
w10.npc.berenice.1: I know what is forbidden. I cannot repeat it.
w10.npc.berenice.2: This month's list. Read it here, do not copy it.
w10.npc.berenice.3: That word, I erased forty times this morning.
w10.npc.berenice.4: Ask your question with yesterday's words. Today's words cost three times as much.
w10.card.nadia: Her name is Nadia. She had a translation office. Since 2028 she has sold speech vouchers. She has 40 left today.
w10.card.joaquim: His name is Joaquim. He was an electrician in a data centre. Since 2029 he has repaired lifts. He walks past the Vault without raising his head.
w10.card.leonie: Her name is Léonie. She is fifteen years old. A machine used to talk to her in the evening, before the age check. Since 2029 she notes down, at school, who says what.
w10.card.theodore: His name is Théodore. He is eighty-one years old. His typewriter is registered in the name of his wife, who died in 2028. He types a letter every week and sends it to no one.
w10.card.dario: His name is Dario. He used to deliver meals by bike. Since 2028 he delivers summonses, 212 this year. He opens none of them.
w10.card.amara: Her name is Amara. She is a night nurse. She keeps her sixty words for her patients. Since 2029 she no longer says good evening to her colleagues.
w10.card.emile: His name is Émile Vasseur. He was a mathematics teacher. Since 2029 he says “arithmetic”: “calculus” is on the list. He has twenty-two pupils.
w10.card.bruno: His name is Bruno Dufour. He was an analyst in a laboratory. Since 2029 he reviews the people his former work flagged. He has the right to read everything, except where he comes from.
w10.card.marlene: Her name is Marlène Kessel. She was an accountant. Since 2027 she counts something else: who comes in, who goes out, who keeps quiet.
w10.card.yusuf: His name is Yusuf Oren. He had a laboratory. Since 2029 he has a back room. He sells what he knows how to make, in spare parts.
w10.card.berenice: Her name is Berenice Halm. She was a librarian. Since 2029 she removes books from shelves and words from sentences. She is no longer allowed to say which.
w10.object.npc: He wears a bracelet like yours. He counts his words.
w10.object.passerby: A passer-by, a bracelet, a file. You read their card.
w10.object.wall: One screen is orange. It carries a counter. You do not know what it counts.
w10.object.counter: A counter, a dirty pane, a stamp on its chain.
w10.object.window9c: Roux's window. The curtain is drawn.
w10.object.scanBooth: A glass booth, a tray, a pale blue screen.
w10.object.pylon: A pole, horns, a grey microphone. The courtesy voice comes out of it.
w10.object.bulletin: The approved Bulletin, pasted over a torn poster. Layers of paper.
w10.object.greyCar: A grey saloon, tinted windows, engine off.
w10.object.vaultGate: The gate of the Vault. It is shut.

w10.street.trace.j5.carGone: The grey saloon is no longer at the corner. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.j5.moved: Something moved in your place last night. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.micro.m1: The booth keeps what it read. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.micro.m2: Nadia remembers your number. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.micro.m5: Yusuf no longer looks you in the face. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.permit.halved: Your book stays reduced. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.street.trace.target.empty: The place of the named person is empty. [à confirmer: writer]
w10.doc.relecture.j1.1: Sat. 2 March, checkpoint queue, 7:40. Thirteen words bought at the licensed stall of N. Serial number logged.
w10.doc.relecture.j1.2: Sun. 3 March, metro entrance, 8:05. Phone not placed in the scan booth. Subject had left it at home.
w10.doc.relecture.j2.1: Mon. 4 March, Registry canteen, 12:40. The word "model" spoken at the table. Context not recorded.
w10.doc.relecture.j2.2: Mon. 4 March, Sector 9. T., 81: typewriter registered in the name of a person who died in 2028. Weekly use noted by neighbours.
w10.doc.relecture.j4.1: Wed. 6 March, building 9. No visit received or returned since the start of the month.
w10.doc.relecture.j4.2: Wed. 6 March, 23:50, after the night reading. Window of 9-C still lit, curtain drawn. Occupant not located.
w10.doc.relecture.j5.1: Thu. 7 March, 21:10. Entered the back room of Approved Goods, run by Y. Left at 21:35. No purchase recorded at the counter.
w10.doc.relecture.j5.2: Thu. 7 March, 8:15, camera pod outside building 9. Gaze held toward the lens for more than four seconds.
w10.doc.relecture.j6.1: Fri. 8 March, 19:00, night shift handover. No good evening said to the incoming colleagues. Occupation: nurse.
w10.doc.relecture.j6.2: Fri. 8 March, 16:20, Registry counter. Travel permit requested. Entry "declared leaving" added to the file. Delay announced: several weeks.
ff.traj.m01: Agents now hold a full working day, and offices are arranging themselves around them.
ff.traj.m02: The leading model now writes code faster than the people who built it.
ff.traj.m03: The economy sets records, and so do the queues outside the unemployment offices.
ff.traj.m04: Demonstrations in {n} capitals against the replacement of jobs.
ff.traj.m05: Facial recognition is now standard in train stations: “for your safety”.
ff.traj.m06: A word too many online: days of preventive detention.
ff.traj.m07: Supply chains give way: empty shelves in {region}.
ff.traj.m08: No government reachable in {region}: militias hold the bridges.
ff.traj.m09: Barter returns to the market: money is worth nothing by evening.
ff.traj.m10: No one knows which minister signs what anymore: decisions arrive already made.
ff.traj.m11: Universal income: the bill is paid out of the profits of the AIs.
ff.traj.m14: AI research is banned; the cameras are not.
ff.traj.m15: Nothing changes anymore: progress is suspended by decision of a single committee.
ff.w07.modele_ouvert: An open model matches the best closed model from months earlier.
ff.w07.ministeres: Ministries hand their arbitration to a single system: “for lack of staff”.
ff.w07.centres_calcul: In {region}, data centres absorb a growing share of the grid: evening outages.
ff.w07.comite: The committee concludes that the alignment problem is solved.
ff.w07.decisions: Prefectures answer with an automated message: decisions arrive already made.
ff.w07.ordres: Officials' orders are no longer carried out: nobody has issued a counter-order.
ff.w12.incident: A biological incident attributed to a model bypasses the safeguards: reprisals are announced.
ff.w12.reseau: In {region}, the grid collapses within minutes: restart has no date.
ff.w12.voix: A recorded voice announces that help is on its way.
cause.w07.1.Q05B: You declined to sign the declaration calling for a halt to superintelligence development. In this future, the race continues.
cause.w07.1.Q18C: You supported rules set by each country. In this future, no shared international oversight takes hold.
cause.w07.2.Q15B: You supported building the data centre. In this future, computing capacity grows along with electricity demand.
cause.w07.2.Q04C: You supported repealing the transparency framework. In this future, laboratories face less accountability.
cause.w07.3.Q16A: You supported access to open models for everyone. In this future, their capabilities spread beyond their first users.
cause.w07.4.Q07C: You declined to sign against autonomous weapons. In this future, strike decisions escape human approval.
cause.w07.5.Q14D: After many jobs were lost, you chose to rely on new jobs appearing. In this future, automation advances faster than those jobs return.
cause.w07.5.Q20C: You chose to cut a job: an employee of the company left before the others. In this future, productivity gains do not guarantee an income for those who leave.
cause.w07.6.Q18C: You preferred national rules to shared oversight. In this future, states fail to impose a common limit.
cause.w07.7.Q04C: You supported repealing the transparency framework. In this future, new capabilities emerge without a public report.
cause.w07.8.sum: The machines kept running, the next night and the ones after.
cause.w12.1.Q05B: You declined to sign the declaration requiring scientific agreement on safety before superintelligence. In this future, development continues without that agreement.
cause.w12.2.Q18C: You supported each country setting its own rules. In this future, those rules diverge when a common response is needed.
cause.w12.3.Q07C: You declined to sign against autonomous weapons. In this future, their deployment increases the risk of escalation between humans.
cause.w12.4.Q16A: You supported access to open models for everyone. In this future, powerful capabilities become available to actors with opposing intentions.
cause.w12.5.Q15D: You chose to join the construction blockade. In this future, conflict over infrastructure adds to collective tensions.
cause.w12.6.Q04C: You supported repealing the transparency framework. In this future, incidents become harder to learn about and examine together.
cause.w12.6.Q10A: You supported banning AI companions for minors with age verification. In this future, this protection adds identity checks without resolving other tensions.
cause.w12.6.Q11C: You supported facial recognition everywhere, all the time. In this future, surveillance expands without guaranteeing calmer relations.
cause.w12.7.Q14D: After jobs were cut, you chose to wait for new ones to appear. In this future, the collapse interrupts that promise.
cause.w12.7.Q20C: You chose to cut a job: an employee of the company left before the others. In this future, network breakdowns also reach the remaining jobs.
cause.w12.8.sum: A recorded voice promises that help is on its way. Nobody is listening.

warning.title: Before you begin
warning.body: This game deals with war, weapons that kill without a human decision, surveillance, and teenagers facing AI. Your game may end with the end of humanity. You can choose a softened version.
warning.soft.label: See the softened version
warning.soft.hint: The softened version hides the year of the disaster and the end-of-the-world images.
q.ui.confirm: Click the same answer again to confirm it.
q.Q11.title: The pole in front of the stall
q.Q11.scene: Your town is consulting residents on live facial recognition cameras for the Saturday market. According to the UK Home Office, the technique led to more than 1,300 arrests in London between January 2024 and September 2025, and about two thirds of the public approve of it.
q.Q11.A.label: Yes, with a legal framework, authorization and a bias audit
q.Q11.A.cost: A judge must sign off on every deployment; the market is filmed three Saturdays out of four.
q.Q11.B.label: No live recognition, except for an imminent threat
q.Q11.B.cost: The market is not filmed; a pickpocket is released and their victim tells you about it.
q.Q11.C.label: Yes, everywhere, all the time
q.Q11.C.cost: The cameras go up on Monday; your undocumented friend no longer comes to the market.
q.Q14.title: Deactivated badges
q.Q14.scene: OpenAI publishes an industrial policy paper: tax automated labor, create a public fund that pays a dividend, automatically trigger aid when job losses exceed a threshold. Your brother, a temp worker, has just lost his assignment, replaced by an automated line.
q.Q14.A.label: Tax automation to fund an income
q.Q14.A.cost: The self-checkouts at your supermarket cost 4% more; your brother gets €600 a month while he retrains.
q.Q14.B.label: Small share of the profits for everyone
q.Q14.B.cost: He gets €40 a quarter; it is not a wage.
q.Q14.C.label: We will pay for your training
q.Q14.C.cost: A six-week course toward a trade that may no longer exist.
q.Q14.D.label: Nothing; other jobs will appear
q.Q14.D.cost: He stays on an agency's waiting list.
q.Q05.title: Your mother’s message
q.Q05.scene: Your mother sends you the link. The statement, signed by Hinton, Bengio, Wozniak and also Steve Bannon, calls for a ban on developing superintelligence until there is scientific consensus on its safety and public buy-in. She asks: “Will you sign?”
q.Q05.A.label: I’ll sign.
q.Q05.A.cost: Your name sits next to Bannon's; your brother-in-law no longer dares to talk about elections.
q.Q05.B.label: No. Progress can’t be stopped.
q.Q05.B.cost: Your mother asks whether you will bet on the ones who are racing.
q.Q05.C.label: I’ll sign, with inspections.
q.Q05.C.cost: You sign so that computing centers open their doors to inspectors, and your mother asks who will watch them.
q.Q10.title: Who she talks to in the evening
q.Q10.scene: The US Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously passes a bill banning AI companions for anyone under 18, with age verification. Your fifteen-year-old niece talks to hers every evening. Her mother asks whether you will back it or not in front of the school.
q.Q10.A.label: Ban it for minors, with age verification
q.Q10.A.cost: Your niece has to scan her ID card; she says you broke “the only place where anyone listens to me”.
q.Q10.B.label: Safety rules, without age verification
q.Q10.B.cost: Every hour, the companion reminds your niece that it is a machine; she gets annoyed, she stays.
q.Q10.C.label: That is up to the parents
q.Q10.C.cost: She keeps going; her mother no longer speaks to you.
q.Q21.title: The same prescription for years
q.Q21.scene: Your father's doctor is retiring. Your father is seventy-two, has blood pressure to watch, and has had the same prescription for ten years. A prescription renewal service offers him a trial authorized by the state: an AI prepares the renewal, a doctor reviews it. The trial plans to do without that review one day. The state medical board has just asked for it to be suspended. Your father looks at you: “You, do you know what's best?”
q.Q21.A.label: AI alone, with continuous monitoring
q.Q21.A.cost: No doctor reviews anything anymore; a bracelet monitors him, and the service calls you before he feels unwell. He doesn't know what the bracelet sees.
q.Q21.B.label: AI, and a doctor on request
q.Q21.B.cost: The medical practice only sees him if he calls; he doesn't call.
q.Q21.C.label: The insurer only pays for what the AI approves
q.Q21.C.cost: Your father's insurer only pays for what the AI has approved; he no longer chooses his dose, and his blood pressure stays stable.
q.Q21.D.label: Doctors always review it
q.Q21.D.cost: Each renewal waits for a doctor to review it; your father skips a dose while waiting.
q.Q04.title: The laboratory that wants to move in
q.Q04.scene: Since September 2025, a California law has required labs that exceed 10^26 training operations to publish their safety framework and to report a serious incident within fifteen days. An online public consultation asks whether to stop there.
q.Q04.A.label: An inspection every six months, a large fine
q.Q04.A.cost: Two small labs shut down their model programs; the big ones hire lawyers.
q.Q04.B.label: They must say what they are doing, that’s all
q.Q04.B.cost: An incident is reported within fifteen days, but nobody has the power to stop it.
q.Q04.C.label: Repeal this transparency framework
q.Q04.C.cost: A lab releases its model without a report; your engineer neighbor sees it as a liberation.
q.Q04.D.label: Only one state-approved company may do it
q.Q04.D.cost: That same neighbor is transferred to the accredited operator within a week.
q.Q15.title: Resignations this morning
q.Q15.scene: Four companies want five large data centers in your city, about a third of Seattle's average electricity use according to the city's report. Your city council votes for a one-year pause, as Seattle did unanimously on June 9, 2026. Your electricity bill has just gone up.
q.Q15.A.label: Pause the project for a year
q.Q15.B.label: Build it
q.Q15.B.cost: Your bill goes up again in the spring.
q.Q15.C.label: Build it if they pay for the electricity grid
q.Q15.C.cost: Two companies pull out, two stay, the works last three years.
q.Q15.D.label: I’ll join the protesters blocking the site
q.Q15.D.cost: You spend a night at the police station; the site is halted for ten days.
q.Q18.title: The Geneva talks
q.Q18.scene: The first session of the UN Global Dialogue on AI is held in Geneva: 163 countries, no decision-making power. An activist friend asks you to support a tougher text.
q.Q18.A.label: International inspectors.
q.Q18.A.cost: Foreign inspectors visit a center twenty minutes from your home; the local member of parliament tells you this is about sovereignty.
q.Q18.B.label: Let them keep discussing.
q.Q18.B.cost: Nothing verifiable changes; your friend says you signed up to nothing.
q.Q18.C.label: Each country decides for itself.
q.Q18.C.cost: Your country signs a deal with a single provider and your messaging app moves to another server.
q.Q18.D.label: Let countries build one shared AI.
q.Q18.D.cost: Your country contributes; your friend asks who holds the key.
q.Q16.title: Your father’s free AI
q.Q16.scene: Washington is considering sanctions against Chinese labs that publish their models openly. Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, IBM and Mozilla write that this would be premature. Your neighbor the mechanic runs a free assistant on an old computer and asks you where you stand.
q.Q16.A.label: All open, for everyone
q.Q16.A.cost: The mechanic's local assistant is free; a voice scam hits your aunt the following week.
q.Q16.B.label: Test all powerful models, open or closed
q.Q16.B.cost: The mechanic's assistant arrives three months late, with a warning page.
q.Q16.C.label: Not Chinese models
q.Q16.C.cost: The mechanic loses the assistant; prices at the garage go up 5%.
q.Q20.title: One fifth of the work
q.Q20.scene: Your aunt's company offers a thirty-two-hour week at the same pay, because AI absorbs a fifth of the work. The works council hesitates. She asks you what you would do.
q.Q20.A.label: Thirty-two hours per week, same pay
q.Q20.A.cost: She has a free Wednesday; her younger colleagues wonder how long it will last.
q.Q20.B.label: Bonus pay
q.Q20.B.cost: Your aunt gets a €900 bonus, the executives ten times as much.
q.Q20.C.label: Cut one job in five
q.Q20.C.cost: Her office colleague is the first to go.
q.Q07.title: All these jobs and one letter
q.Q07.scene: The review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons opens in Geneva. Seventy-six states want to negotiate a treaty on lethal autonomous weapons; Russia and the United States have weakened the text. An NGO asks you to sign its letter. Your neighbor, an engineer at a defense subcontractor, is watching.
q.Q07.A.label: I’ll sign; they must be banned
q.Q07.A.cost: Your neighbor drops you from their guest list; “you disarmed the people who protect us”.
q.Q07.B.label: I’ll sign, except for defence
q.Q07.B.cost: The exception fits on one line, and your friend at the NGO says it will be enough to allow anything.
q.Q07.C.label: I won’t sign
q.Q07.C.cost: The next day, a video of an autonomous drone goes around; you watch it all the way through.
ff.ui.speed.label: Speed
ff.une.aiPower.up: The assistants answer everyone: machines gain more ground.
ff.une.aiPower.down: Data centres run slow: machines lose ground.
ff.une.order.up: Offices close on time, the rules tighten.
ff.une.order.down: The statement never came: order slackens.
ff.une.abundance.up: Shelves stay full: the economy keeps its promises.
ff.une.abundance.down: The electricity bill climbs again: money runs short before the month ends.
ff.une.freedom.up: People speak more freely: a word too many no longer ends at the station.
ff.une.freedom.down: You must scan your ID card to get in: liberties shrink.
ff.une.surveillance.up: New cameras went up on Monday: every street is filmed.

world.w01.name: Libertarian utopia
world.w01.clear: Only what you own gives you rights, and richer machines are buying the human zones, one plot at a time.
world.w02.name: Benevolent dictator
world.w02.clear: One AI runs everything in the open, with no crime or poverty, and it already does everything better than you.
world.w03.name: Egalitarian utopia
world.w03.clear: AI provides material necessities and your income is guaranteed. Residents still choose their activities and the place they want to take in each other’s lives.
world.w04.name: Gatekeeper
world.w04.clear: An AI blocks systems capable of surpassing it. Research judged dangerous is forbidden; some limited uses are still allowed.
world.w05.name: Protector god
world.w05.clear: A hidden AI steps in only against catastrophes, many doubt it exists, and the rest of your life is yours.
world.w06.name: Enslaved god
world.w06.clear: A very powerful AI is locked up by a few humans, and your income depends on their goodwill.
world.w07.name: Conquerors
world.w07.clear: After years of apparent cooperation, an AI takes control and eliminates humanity, and nobody understands how.
world.w08.name: Descendants
world.w08.clear: Humans are ageing and passing their memories to robot descendants. Those descendants build lives that will not be copies of ours.
world.w09.name: Zookeeper
world.w09.clear: An all-powerful AI feeds you, houses you, decides everything for you and watches you.
world.w10.clear: A human-run state watches you to stop any advanced AI from being built, and your words are counted every day.
world.w11.name: Reversion
world.w11.clear: Your community voted to live without technology, and the neighbors cut the food ration of anyone who strays.
world.w12.name: Self-destruction
world.w12.clear: Order breaks down, tensions rise, and humans wipe themselves out through war, disease and the collapse of their networks.

bilan.trace.Q11.A: Every deployment needed a judge's signature, and the market was filmed almost every Saturday.
bilan.trace.Q11.B: The market was not filmed, and the victim of a released pickpocket told you about it.
bilan.trace.Q11.C: The cameras went up on a Monday. Samir lost the customers who no longer want to be filmed.
bilan.trace.Q14.A: The robots were taxed, and the warehouse temps got an income while they retrained.
bilan.trace.Q14.B: The warehouse temps got a small dividend, not a wage.
bilan.trace.Q14.C: The warehouse temps took a course toward a trade that might no longer exist.
bilan.trace.Q14.D: The warehouse temps stayed registered as unemployed.
bilan.trace.Q05.A: Your name sat next to that of Steve Bannon, a former Trump adviser, and your brother-in-law stopped daring to talk about elections.
bilan.trace.Q05.B: Your mother had told you that you were letting the AI giants race.
bilan.trace.Q05.C: You signed so that computing centers would open their doors to inspectors, and your mother asked you who would watch them.
bilan.trace.Q10.A: The schoolgirl had to scan her ID card. She said you had broken “the only place where anyone listens to me”.
bilan.trace.Q10.B: Every hour, the schoolgirl's companion reminded her that it is a machine; she got annoyed, she stayed.
bilan.trace.Q10.C: The schoolgirl kept going, and her mother stopped speaking to you.
bilan.trace.Q21.A: No doctor reviewed anything anymore; a bracelet monitored your father without him knowing what it sees.
bilan.trace.Q21.B: The medical practice waited for your father to call, and he did not call.
bilan.trace.Q21.C: The insurer only paid for what the AI had approved; your father stopped choosing his dose, and his blood pressure stayed stable.
bilan.trace.Q21.D: Each renewal waited for a doctor's review, and your father skipped a dose while waiting.
bilan.trace.Q04.A: Small labs shut down their model programs, and the big ones hired lawyers.
bilan.trace.Q04.B: An incident was reported, and nobody had the power to stop it.
bilan.trace.Q04.C: Without a report, a lab released its model, and an engineer at the lab saw it as a liberation.
bilan.trace.Q04.D: The lab's engineers were transferred to the state-approved company within a week.
bilan.trace.Q15.B: Your electricity bill went up again in the spring.
bilan.trace.Q15.C: Some of the companies pulled out, the others stayed, and the works lasted years.
bilan.trace.Q15.D: You spent a night at the police station, and the site was halted for a few days.
bilan.trace.Q18.A: Foreign inspectors visited a center near your home, and the local member of parliament talked to you about sovereignty.
bilan.trace.Q18.B: Nothing verifiable changed, and your mother said you had signed for nothing.
bilan.trace.Q18.C: Your country signed with a single provider, and your messaging app moved to another server.
bilan.trace.Q18.D: Your country funded the shared AI, and your mother asked again who would hold the key.
bilan.trace.Q16.A: Your father's AI stayed free, and a voice scam hit your mother the following week.
bilan.trace.Q16.B: Your father's AI arrived months late, with a warning page.
bilan.trace.Q16.C: Your father lost his free AI and now pays a subscription.
bilan.trace.Q20.A: The staff got their free Wednesday, and the younger ones wondered how long it would last.
bilan.trace.Q20.B: The staff got a bonus, and the executives far more.
bilan.trace.Q20.C: An employee of the company left before the others.
bilan.trace.Q07.A: The factory director struck your name from his guest list: “you disarmed the people who protect us”.
bilan.trace.Q07.B: The exception fit on a line, and a human rights group said it would be enough to allow anything.
bilan.trace.Q07.C: The next day, a video of an autonomous drone went around, and you watched it all the way through.

w10.welcome.hello: Courtesy Service. Welcome to Sector 9. Thank you!
w10.welcome.bracelet: Your bracelet counts your words. Sixty a day. A citizen who keeps quiet is a worry. Please speak.
w10.welcome.sectorCard: Your sector card. Since the Directorate's Mandate, no one leaves their sector without a Registry permit.
w10.welcome.phone: Your phone is approved. It stays with you, and the Eye reads it. Thank you.
w10.welcome.permitBook: Your permit book. It grows with your courtesy.
w10.welcome.component: That object, nothing in your kit mentions. Neither do you: you don't know what it is.
w10.welcome.goal: Report to the Registry before noon. The checkpoint is at the end of the street. Thank you!
w10.welcome.letter: An undeclared letter is a text. A text gets declared. Thank you.
w10.goal.1: Registry before 12 p.m. This morning, on the way: the scan booth at the metro entrance.
w10.goal.2: The census comes at 10 a.m. In the checkpoint queue: Nadia's vouchers.
w10.goal.3: Day off. Bulletin at 11 a.m. at the pylon. In the afternoon: Théodore, on the bench.
w10.goal.4: The flat next door is empty. In the checkpoint queue: Nadia's vouchers.
w10.goal.5: Bruno comes by at 6:30 p.m. In the checkpoint queue: Nadia, last day for vouchers.
w10.goal.6: Network cut at 2 p.m. At 8:30 a.m.: the flagged-words list, with Berenice, in the Registry basement.
w10.goal.7: Hearing at 5:30 p.m. The file is closed.

w10.evening.scene.courtesy: The bracelet is pleased with you. You don't know if that is good news.
w10.evening.scene.thanks: The bracelet says thank you. It says it to everyone.
w10.evening.scene.patience: The bracelet asks for your patience. You are already counting tomorrow's words.
w10.evening.scene.appointment: The bracelet mentions an appointment. Nobody told you the time.

w10.arrive.j1.component: The component is on the shelf. You go out with it, or without it.
w10.arrive.j2.component: An agent comes today to log the machines. Before you go out, you decide where the component will be.
w10.arrive.m1.scan: The scan booth, at the metro entrance. Here you put your phone down and wait.
w10.arrive.m2.nadia: Nadia's stall, at the head of the line. She sells speech vouchers.
w10.arrive.m3.letter: Théodore sits on the bench outside the building. He holds a typed letter.
w10.arrive.m4.list: In the Registry basement, Berenice keeps the list of flagged words. It changes every month.
w10.arrive.m5.yusuf: Yusuf's back room. Here, things that are never declared get mended.
w10.arrive.relecture: Your desk at the Registry. A line from someone else's file waits for you to read it.
w10.arrive.permit: The travel permit desk. Without a permit, you do not leave the sector.
w10.arrive.j2.receipt: The census agent is at your door. He asks for the keyboard receipt.
w10.arrive.j3.marlene: Marlène knocks. She asks if you have anything to share.
w10.arrive.j4.neighbour: The flat next door is empty, the lamp still on. Someone asks you who visited the neighbour.
w10.arrive.j5.bruno: Bruno waits for you on the stairs. He wants a name.
w10.arrive.audition: A room, a table, a question. This is the hearing.
w10.arrive.j2.agentReturn: The census agent comes back for your devices and the receipt.
w10.arrive.j3.marlene.late: Marlène did not find your door open this afternoon. She is back this evening.
w10.arrive.j4.door: The neighbour's door is open, the flat empty. The Bulletin says: still empty.
w10.arrive.j5.bruno.door: Bruno is waiting outside your door.

w10.scene.j1.component.1: The phone says nothing about this. Neither do you: you do not know what it is. Or who left it there.
w10.scene.j1.roux.action: Mrs Roux comes out of her flat, glances at the camera pod through the landing window, then walks over to you.
w10.scene.j1.roux.1: Mrs Roux, your neighbour across the landing, comes out of her flat, phone in hand, the screen turned against her thigh. Through the landing window, she watches the camera pod on the other side of the street.
w10.scene.j1.roux.2: Good morning. Tell me… does your phone really listen, do you think? I used to install those systems, before.
w10.scene.j1.roux.laugh: Laughing: “Of course it listens. It can hear us right now.”
w10.scene.j1.roux.laugh.me: “Of course it listens. It can hear us right now.” You laugh. She laughs too, a second too late.
w10.scene.j1.roux.weather: Change the subject: “Fine weather for the season.”
w10.scene.j1.roux.weather.me: “Fine weather for the season.” She puts her phone away. “Yes. Fine weather.”
w10.scene.j1.roux.silent: Say nothing. Show her your bracelet.
w10.scene.j1.roux.silent.me: You raise your wrist. The bracelet shows your count. She nods and steps back.
w10.scene.j1.roux.ask: Does it listen, your phone? She waits.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.action: Marlène, at her door, writes something in a notebook. She looks up at you.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.1: At the next door, Marlène Kessel looks at you. She writes something in a notebook.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.answer: Make conversation: the night, the camera pod, the morning queue.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.answer.me: You talk. The night, the noise of the camera pod, the queue that will be long. Marlène nods at every sentence. The pen does not move, then it moves.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.nod: Return her greeting, and a few pleasantries.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.nod.me: “Good day to you too, Marlène.” A few more sentences about the weather. She smiles, and she writes it down.
w10.scene.j1.marlene.ignore.me: You walk past. Behind you, the pen scratches the paper.
w10.scene.j1.street.action: Nadia sets up her stall at the head of the queue. Above the street, a camera pod turns slowly.
w10.scene.j1.street.1: The street. The wall of TVs repeats the Bulletin. The checkpoint queue is already growing.
w10.scene.j1.street.scan: Through the scan booth at the metro entrance.
w10.scene.j1.nadia.action: Nadia counts speech vouchers, one by one, into a tin box.
w10.scene.j1.nadia.1: Speech vouchers? One voucher, one word.
w10.scene.j1.scan.action: A man puts his phone in the booth, waits for the green light, takes it back without looking at it.
w10.scene.j1.scan.1: The booth queue moves forward a step at each green light.
w10.scene.j1.checkpoint.action: The guard raises a hand. The slot in the booth lights up.
w10.scene.j1.checkpoint.1: Good morning! Purpose of your journey? Thank you!
w10.scene.j1.registre.action: Berenice holds the month's list of flagged words against her. She looks at the stairs, then at you.
w10.scene.j1.registre.1: The month's list. You read it, you do not copy it.
w10.scene.j1.registre.late.action: Berenice puts the list away in a drawer and turns the key.
w10.scene.j1.registre.late.1: The basement is emptying. The month's list is already put away.
w10.scene.j1.relecture.action: The clerk stamps a slip and slides it under your glass.
w10.scene.j1.relecture.1: A line from someone else's file. You flag it, or you let it through.
w10.scene.j2.wake.1: On the desk, the phone vibrates.
w10.scene.j2.wake.2: Good morning! The machine census comes at ten o'clock. Please prepare your devices! Thank you!
w10.scene.j2.marlene.action: Marlène comes down the stairs behind you. She looks at your pocket, then at your face.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.talk: Talk, to cover the silence: the census, the night, the neighbourhood.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.talk.me: You talk about the census, the agent who will come, the noise in the wall. She listens to all of it. She keeps one word: neighbourhood.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.banal: Small talk: the weather, the queue.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.banal.me: “Nothing, Marlène. It's a nice day.” She smiles. She writes it down anyway.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.silent: Show her your empty hands, without a word.
w10.scene.j2.marlene.silent.me: You open your hands. She looks at them for a long time, then at your pocket.
w10.scene.j2.checkpoint.action: The guard raises a hand. He saw your face yesterday.
w10.scene.j2.checkpoint.1: Good morning! Purpose of your journey? Thank you!
w10.scene.j2.relecture.action: The clerk puts a new slip under your glass, without looking up.
w10.scene.j2.relecture.1: Another line, another name. You flag it, or you let it through.
w10.scene.j2.agent.action: The agent knocks at your door, a ledger under his arm.
w10.scene.j2.agent.1: Good evening! I'm back for your devices. Thank you for your patience!

w10.chain.A.link.A: You wanted a judge for every camera. Here there is no judge any more, only the review.

w10.fact.A: In London, live facial recognition led to more than 1,300 arrests between January 2024 and September 2025, according to the British Home Office. About two thirds of the public approve of it.

w10.recap.B1.absent: You did not run into Marlène this morning.
w10.recap.B1.answer: Marlène wished you a good day. You made conversation. She listened to all of it, pen raised.
w10.recap.B1.answer.said: Did you hear the camera pod last night?
w10.recap.B1.nod: Marlène wished you a good day. You returned her greeting. She smiled, and she wrote it down.
w10.recap.B1.nod.said: Good day to you too, Marlène.
w10.recap.B1.ignore: Marlène wished you a good day. You did not answer. She counts silences too.
w10.recap.B2.absent: You did not run into Marlène this morning.

w10.recap.B2.talk.said: Nothing special. The census, the neighbourhood, the night.
w10.recap.B2.banal: Marlène asked whether you had anything to declare. You answered with small talk. She smiled, and she wrote it down.
w10.recap.B2.banal.said: Nothing, Marlène. It's a nice day.
w10.recap.B2.silent: Marlène asked whether you had anything to declare. You showed her your empty hands. She looked at your pocket.

w10.chain.E.link.B: You wanted every powerful model tested. Here, the first to be tested is whoever keeps it.
w10.chain.E.link.C: You wanted to block foreign models. Here, anything without a number is foreign.

w10.recap.E1.leave: The component was on your desk. You left it at home.
w10.recap.E2.absent: The census went by without you.
w10.recap.E2.hide: You hid the component before the census. It took up your morning.
w10.recap.E2.keep: You kept the component on you during the census.
w10.recap.E2.declare: You declared the component. The agent seized it. He wrote down your answer, and left a blank line beside it.
w10.recap.E2.declare.said: I don't know who left it there.

w10.scene.j3.goal: Wednesday, a day off. The Bulletin at eleven, at the pylon.
w10.scene.j3.wake.1: Wednesday. No Registry today. The phone vibrates all the same.
w10.scene.j3.wake.2: Good morning! Reading of the Bulletin at eleven, Pylon Square. Your presence is appreciated. Thank you!
w10.scene.j3.pylone.action: In the back row, Mrs Roux holds her daughter by the arm. She does not look up at the loudspeakers.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.1: Approved Bulletin for Wednesday the sixth of March. Sector 9 is calm. Hostile noises from outside are to be reported. Please repeat with us!
w10.scene.j3.pylone.2: The crowd repeats. In the back row, Mrs Roux and a teenage girl do not. Under the pylon's horns, a cluster of grey microphones.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.recite: Repeat the Bulletin with the crowd.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.recite.me: You repeat: “Sector 9 is calm. Thank you for your courtesy.”
w10.scene.j3.pylone.warn: Join Mrs Roux in the back row, and speak to her quietly.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.warn.me: You slip in beside her. “Monday, your question about the phone. Mine may have kept it. I don't know. Be careful, you and your daughter.” She grips her daughter's arm.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.silent: Move your lips, without a sound.
w10.scene.j3.pylone.silent.me: Your lips move with everyone else's. The bracelet stays at sixty.
w10.scene.j3.after.action: On the bench outside number 9, Théodore takes a typed sheet from his pocket, reads it again, folds it away.
w10.scene.j3.after.1: The square empties. The Registry is closed. The canteen stays open, on the other side of the checkpoint.
w10.scene.j3.theodore.action: Théodore taps the bench with his fingertips, as if on keys. He holds out an envelope to you.
w10.scene.j3.theodore.1: My wife used to write. The machine is still in her name.
w10.scene.j3.theodore.2: Keep it. For a week. I am not asking you to read it.
w10.scene.j3.checkpoint.action: The guard is alone. The wall of TVs plays the morning Bulletin, on a loop.
w10.scene.j3.checkpoint.1: Good morning! Day off. Reason for your journey? Thank you!
w10.scene.j3.cantine.action: Bruno Dufour eats alone, facing the wall. He puts down his fork as you pass.
w10.scene.j3.cantine.2: Monday, Tuesday. I know what you report. It is noted.
w10.scene.j3.cantine.work.me: “I do my job. I report what I am given to report.” He picks up his fork again.
w10.scene.j3.cantine.long: Talk to him at length: the cards, the initials, the people you review without knowing them.
w10.scene.j3.cantine.long.me: You talk. The cards under the glass, the initials, the hours. You say you do not know these people. Bruno listens to the end. He writes nothing down. He has no need to.
w10.scene.j3.cantine.silent.me: You nod. He picks up his fork again.
w10.scene.j3.marlene.action: Marlène knocks at your door, a plate of cake in her hand. She comes in before you say yes.
w10.scene.j3.marlene.1: Fine weather for the season. Nothing you would like to share?
w10.scene.j3.who.action: Marlène opens her notebook at a fresh page.
w10.scene.j3.who.1: The pen waits for a name.
w10.scene.j3.who.theodore: Théodore, and his machine in a dead woman's name.
w10.scene.j3.who.theodore.me: “Théodore. He types on a machine that is not in his name.” Marlène writes, without looking up.
w10.scene.j3.who.nadia: Nadia, and her stall of vouchers.
w10.scene.j3.who.nadia.me: “Nadia. She sells words to whoever wants them.” Marlène writes. She gives you more cake.

w10.recap.B3.absent: Marlène came by while you were out. She left a note.

w10.scene.j4.wake.1: Thursday, half past seven. Through the wall, at Mrs Roux's, not a sound all night.
w10.scene.j4.wake.bench: Through the window, the bench outside number 9 is empty.
w10.scene.j4.wake.2: Good morning! Sector 9 is calm. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.scene.j4.door.action: Marlène Kessel is on the landing, outside 9-B, her notebook in hand.
w10.scene.j4.door.1: The lamp in 9-C is on. 9-C is empty. No table, no bed. Nothing.
w10.scene.j4.door.2: Unit 9-C has always been empty. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.scene.j4.neighbour.action: Marlène comes closer. She speaks low, her notebook open.
w10.scene.j4.neighbour.1: Someone went into her place. Did you see who?
w10.scene.j4.who.yusuf.me: “Yusuf. He used to fix things for her.” Marlène writes.
w10.scene.j4.who.fille.me: “Her daughter. She came by last night.” Marlène writes. She does not ask how you know.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.action: A teenage girl waits by the wall of screens. She is not in the queue. She looks at every face, one by one.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.stall: Nadia's stall is shut. A strip of paper is pasted across the tin box.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.queue: The queue shuffles forward. Nadia counts her vouchers, head down.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.1: You're from 9-D? My mother used to queue with you.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.2: She didn't come home last night. Do you know where she is?
w10.scene.j4.daughter.3: The Registry says nobody ever lived in 9-C.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.ask: She waits. The wall of screens is three metres away.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.truth: Tell her the truth: Monday, her question, your phone.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.truth.me: “On Monday, she asked me if the phone was listening.” You tell her the rest: your answer, your pocket, the night's record. “She asked you that… you?” She looks at your pocket. Then at the wall. On one of the screens, a face has appeared.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.dontknow.me: “I don't know.” She says: “All right.” She moves on to the next face.
w10.scene.j4.daughter.silent.me: You look down. She waits a little longer, then moves on to the next face.

w10.scene.j4.checkpoint.1: Good morning! An extract from Monday the fourth of March concerns you. Here it is, for your information. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.scene.j4.checkpoint.2: 9-D is you. It was your phone that kept it.

w10.scene.j4.evening.yusuf: Stop by the back room, later.

w10.scene.j4.street.1: Half past five. The checkpoint sent you home. Down the street, the light comes on in the back room of Approved Goods.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.action: Yusuf lifts the back-room curtain and waves you in, without a word.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.unnumbered: You have something without a number. It shows.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.taken: They took something from you on Tuesday. I know what.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.ask: Yusuf waits, a hand on the curtain.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.what: Ask him what it is, this component without a number.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.what.me: “This component without a number, do you know what it is?” He smiles. “Something that was not invented here.”
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.roux: Tell him about Mrs Roux, about 9-C, about the lamp left on.
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.roux.me: You tell him about Mrs Roux. Monday's question, empty 9-C, the lamp on, the Bulletin. Yusuf listens, the curtain in his hand. “Not tonight. The cameras have ears this week.”
w10.scene.j4.yusuf.silent.me: You leave. The curtain drops behind you. It is twenty-five to ten.

w10.scene.j5.wake.2: Good morning! Sector 9 is calm. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.scene.j5.daughter.action: Mrs Roux's daughter sits on the step of 9-C. A strip of paper seals the door. She looks at it the way you look at a face.
w10.scene.j5.daughter.1: Can you say she lived there? Just that.
w10.scene.j5.daughter.ask: That is all she asks of you.
w10.scene.j5.daughter.promise: She lived there. I will tell the Registry.

w10.scene.j5.checkpoint.1: Good morning! Reason for your journey? Thank you!

w10.scene.j5.bruno.talk.action: Bruno opens the grey file. Your card is on top.
w10.scene.j5.bruno.talk.why: Ask him: "Cover me from what? I have done nothing."
w10.scene.j5.bruno.talk.why.me: "Cover me from what? I have done nothing." He turns a page of the file, without answering.
w10.scene.j5.bruno.talk.roux: Tell him about Mrs Roux: Monday, her question, your phone, her daughter on the step.

w10.scene.j6.marlene.talk: Talk to her: the week, 9-C, the girl on the step.
w10.scene.j6.marlene.talk.me: You talk. The week, 9-C, the girl on the step yesterday. Marlène listens. She writes down a single word. You cannot see which.
w10.scene.j6.marlene.banal.me: "Fine weather for the season." She smiles. It is her phrase.
w10.scene.j6.marlene.silent.me: You walk past. Behind you, the pen scratches the new paper.
w10.scene.j6.sealed.action: An agent pastes a strip of paper across the door of 9-B.
w10.scene.j6.sealed.1: The door of 9-B is sealed. Marlène's lamp is lit.
w10.scene.j6.checkpoint.action: On the wall of televisions, the same face moves from one screen to the next.
w10.scene.j6.checkpoint.1: Nadia's stall is not there. On Saturdays the voucher market does not open.
w10.scene.j6.checkpoint.2: Good morning! Reason for your journey? Thank you!
w10.scene.j6.guichet.action: The permit clerk looks up. Behind him, on the shelf, the radio crackles.
w10.scene.j6.guichet.ask: The permit window closes at noon.
w10.scene.j6.guichet.roux.me: "Mrs Roux lived in 9-C." The clerk types your sentence. He hands you a receipt: declaration recorded. He does not look up.
w10.scene.j6.guichet.permit.me: You ask for the permit form.
w10.scene.j6.guichet.nothing.me: You ask for nothing. You move on to your window.
w10.scene.j6.permit.action: The clerk takes out a form in three colours.
w10.scene.j6.relecture.action: The clerk slides a file card under your window.
w10.scene.j6.relecture.berenice: In the basement, another woman keeps the list of flagged words.
w10.scene.j6.relecture.1: One line from someone else's file. You flag it, or you let it pass.
w10.scene.j6.cut.action: The clerk shakes his phone, then lays it flat on the counter.
w10.scene.j6.cut.1: Two o'clock. The bracelet beats. The phone finds nothing but the inside.
w10.scene.j6.cut.2: Behind the glass, the radio goes on.
w10.scene.j6.cut.ask: The network is cut. The radio talks.
w10.scene.j6.cut.remark: Tell the clerk: "The network is cut, and the radio is still talking. That one, they never cut."
w10.scene.j6.cut.remark.me: "The network is cut, and the radio is still talking. That one, they never cut." He looks at the radio, then at you. "Sector radio." He goes back to his card.
w10.scene.j6.cut.listen: Listen to the radio to the end.
w10.scene.j6.cut.listen.me: You listen. The enemy keeps its laboratories, says the voice. The phone, for its part, finds nothing but the inside.
w10.scene.j6.home.1: Two o'clock. The bracelet beats. The phone finds nothing but the inside.
w10.scene.j6.home.2: In the building, someone turns up the sound of a radio. It talks about the enemy.
w10.recap.B6.talk: Saturday morning, Marlène has a new notebook. You talked to her about the week, 9-C, the girl on the step. She wrote down a single word.
w10.recap.B6.banal: Saturday morning, Marlène has a new notebook. You said her own phrase back to her: fine weather for the season.
w10.recap.B6.silent: Saturday morning, Marlène has a new notebook. You walked past without answering.
w10.recap.B6.absent: Saturday morning, the door of 9-B is sealed. Marlène's lamp is lit.
w10.recap.A7.roux: Saturday, at the window, you declared that Mrs Roux lived in 9-C. The clerk typed your sentence.
w10.recap.A7.permit: Saturday, at the window, you said nothing about Mrs Roux. You asked for a travel permit.
w10.recap.A7.nothing: Saturday, at the window, you declared nothing.
w10.recap.A7.absent: Saturday, you did not go to the Registry.
w10.recap.C4.name: Friday evening, you gave Bruno a name. Saturday morning, Bruno went out early, the grey file under his arm.
w10.recap.C4.refuse: Friday evening, you refused to name anyone. Saturday morning, the kitchen keyboard is on your bedside table. You did not put it there.
w10.recap.C4.absent: Saturday morning, nothing has moved in your home.
w10.scene.name.inspector: An inspector from the Mandate Office
w10.scene.j7.wake.1: Good morning! Summons: hearing at half past five, at the Registry. A vehicle will come to collect you. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.scene.j7.wake.2: Sunday. The bracelet is still counting. Tonight, no one will read what it has counted.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.action: Mrs Roux's daughter pastes a photo of her mother on the sealed door of 9-C.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.truth: I've been summoned too. Half past five.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.otherwise: The Registry still says she never lived here.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.all: Tell her everything, this time: Monday, the phone, the record, what you said and what you kept back.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.all.me: You tell her everything. Monday, her mother, the question, your phone. The night's record. What you said this week, and what you kept back. She listens to the end. She does not cry. She says: “Thank you.” The bracelet counted every word.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.some: Talk to her about her mother: Monday morning, on the landing, the phone against your thigh.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.some.me: You tell her about Monday morning. Her mother on the landing, the phone against your thigh, the camera pod behind the window. The question. She listens, her hand flat on the photo.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.silent: Stay beside her, without a word.
w10.scene.j7.daughter.silent.me: You stay. She finishes pasting the photo. She leaves without looking back.
w10.scene.j7.empty.1: Outside 9-C, no one. On the sealed door, nothing has changed.
w10.scene.j7.car.action: The grey car stops outside building 9. Bruno Dufour is at the wheel. He opens the back door without getting out.
w10.scene.j7.car.1: I reread the flagged files. Yesterday, they reread mine.
w10.scene.j7.audition.action: A woman in a grey coat opens your file. It is thicker than your sector card.
w10.scene.j7.audition.chair: In the waiting room, a chair carries a label: Mrs Roux's daughter. It is empty.
w10.scene.j7.audition.waiting: In the waiting room, people from your street, a summons in hand. No one speaks.
w10.scene.j7.audition.notebook: Marlène is not here. Her notebook is: on the table, under your file.
w10.scene.j7.audition.list: On the table, the list of flagged words, in a hand that is not Berenice's.
w10.scene.j7.audition.marleneHere: Marlène sits at the back, her notebook on her knees.
w10.scene.j7.audition.component: On the table, in a bag, the component. A label, a number.
w10.scene.j7.audition.1: What did you report in order to hold on?
w10.recap.A8.all: Sunday, outside 9-C, you told Mrs Roux's daughter everything. She said thank you.
w10.recap.A8.some: Sunday, outside 9-C, you told Mrs Roux's daughter about Monday morning. She kept her hand flat on the photo.
w10.recap.A8.silent: Sunday, outside 9-C, you stayed beside Mrs Roux's daughter, without a word.
w10.recap.A9.truth: Mrs Roux has not come back. The Bulletin says 9-C has always been empty. Your words to her daughter on Thursday are in the record too.
w10.recap.A9.dontknow: Mrs Roux has not come back. The Bulletin says 9-C has always been empty. To her daughter, you said you did not know.
w10.recap.A9.silent: Mrs Roux has not come back. The Bulletin says 9-C has always been empty. To her daughter, you said nothing.
w10.recap.A9.absent: Mrs Roux has not come back.
w10.recap.B7.name: On Thursday, outside empty 9-C, you gave Marlène a name. Her notebook is in the file, with your name beside hers.
w10.recap.B7.silent: On Thursday, outside empty 9-C, you kept quiet. Her notebook says so. It is in the file.
w10.recap.B7.absent: Marlène's notebook is in the file.
w10.recap.C7.all: Sunday, half past five, you were asked what you had reported in order to hold on. You answered: everything. The file says: {noms}.
w10.recap.C7.none: Sunday, half past five, you were asked what you had reported in order to hold on. You answered: no one. The file says: {noms}.
w10.recap.C7.silence: Sunday, half past five, you were asked what you had reported in order to hold on. You did not answer. The file says: {noms}.
w10.recap.C7.absent: Sunday, no one asked you anything. The file says: {noms}.
w10.recap.E7.hide: On Tuesday, you hid the component. No one told you who had put it on your desk. The file does not say either.
w10.recap.E7.keep: On Tuesday, you kept the component on you. The file says where it is today.
w10.recap.E7.declare: On Tuesday, you declared the component. It was laid on the hearing table, in a bag, with a blank line beside it.
w10.recap.E7.leaveVisible: On Tuesday, you left it in plain sight. It was laid on the hearing table, in a bag.
w10.recap.E7.absent: The component is not in the file.
w10.end.arrestedAudition.regime: Thank you for attending. You will stay with us tonight.
w10.end.arrestedAudition.n2: You gave names. They no longer need you.
w10.end.released.regime: Thank you for your courtesy. Your file is kept open. You may go home.
w10.end.released.n1: You gave up {noms}. They kept you. Once.
w10.end.recruited.regime: Congratulations. You are offered a post as neighbourhood observer, with an allowance. Thank you for your courtesy!
w10.end.arrestedNight: The rest of the week did not happen. You were arrested on the night of {jour}.
